newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Sateras sees lower profit in 97.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Sateras sees lower profit in 97.

text.p: Malaysian diversified company Sateras Resources (Malaysia) Bhd said on Friday it expected its profits for the year ending March 31, 1997 to be lower than those for the previous year.
Sateras managing director Mohamed Kamal Hussain told Reuters he expected the group's net profit to be around six million ringgit, compared to 7.11 million for the year ended March 31, 1996.
"Our profits for this year will be nothing spectacular. They will be quite similar to last year," said Mohamed Kamal.
"Our agreement to sell our Cosmo City development (in the southern Malaysian city of Johor Baru) to MBf Land has been rescinded. Instead we will be developing the property ourselves," he said.
MBf Land is a unit of MBf Holdings Bhd.
Mohamed did not give any projections for 1998, but said that several projects which the company is embarking on will begin to have an impact on earnings in that year.
The Cosmo City development comprises a commercial and shopping complex, and a private college.

Shares of Sateras have been suspended since Wednesday prior to the announcement of the acquisition of land and a cement plant in the northeastern state of Kelantan. The stock was last traded at 2.11 ringgit.
Mohamed Kamal said the shares would be requoted on January 22.
